correctness.rationale: Complete split clique/independent induced-cut classification; orthogonal products and exact spanning-tree volumes give all facet areas and total volume. Exact binomial reweighting and fixed-clique Taylor bounds establish \(O_p(q^{-5/2})\) correction. Endpoint-dominated Stirling summation establishes the convergent \(C_*\) coefficient. The independent convex-hull checker measures 156 facets (82 for \(p\ge3\)) and four spanning-tree enumerations, plus stable finite-ratio tests; finite checks only corroborate the proof. Domains \(p\ge3\), \(q\ge2\), inherited Euclidean unit-root generators, fixed-p asymptotic and iterated p limit explicitly stated.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text sources supply only the connected-cut combinatorial description and a tree enumerator. Compared published-finding corpus records on the identical graph family, complete-multipartite zonotopes, and related bipartite surface-area calculations: none checked provides the variable complete-split facet-area distribution or large-clique Poisson endpoint constant. The common \(3/2\) concentration exponent was already known in a different biclique family; this work adds the all-clique coefficient family and limiting series, not a claimed novel exponent. Unindexed equivalence remains a real risk.
residual_risks: General facet-area identities make the finite calculation possible in principle; the originality rests primarily on an evaluated two-level asymptotic, not on inventing the graph-cut identity.

value.rationale: Complete Euclidean facet-area invariant of an infinite natural (p,q) polytope family; a vanishing exponentially small fraction of facets captures almost all area, with sharp polynomial deficit for every clique size \(p\ge3\). Variable explicit \(A_p\) and an endpoint-Poisson constant approximately \(0.6186033\) reveal new nontrivial p-dependence not available from a one-size example. The exact geometry and asymptotic are motivated by the disagreement between facet-count and area-weighted sampling; no general downstream theorem is needed.
